title: Circular Polarization 1D
full_prompt: Write a complete ManimGL script that visualizes circular polarization in 1D. The scene should feature a charged particle moving in a circular path in the XY plane, and a series of electric field vectors distributed along a perpendicular propagation axis (e.g., the Z-axis or X-axis). These vectors must represent the radiative electric field (Lorentz force / acceleration-dependent field) produced by the particle, taking into account the finite speed of light propagation delay. Implement a custom `ChargedParticle` class that tracks its position and acceleration history, and a custom vector field or set of vectors that update dynamically using updaters. The camera should rotate in 3D space to clearly show the helical, three-dimensional nature of the circularly polarized wave propagating away from the source particle.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Incorrect calculation of retarded time leading to discontinuous or non-propagating waves
common_failure_modes.note: The delay calculation must correctly use the distance from the particle's past positions divided by the speed of light.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Vector field arrows blowing up to infinity near the source particle
common_failure_modes.note: Implement an adjusted norm or softening parameter to prevent division by zero near the particle's center.

common_failure_modes.pattern: Static camera angle failing to reveal the 3D helical structure of circular polarization
common_failure_modes.note: Ensure the 3D camera rotates or is positioned at an oblique angle to show both the circular motion and the linear propagation.
